messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Robotaxi adoption: 7%.

Business closing: Zoe Martinez — close at least one paying social media client this week. the target is betty kowalski's diner first - she is in my inbox, she is stressed and making changes, she is attended by both my network and community organizers. i walk in this week, not call. i sit down when it is not rush hour. i say directly: spending is down 70% from baseline, foot traffic is soft, and i can maintain a humanly present social media account for your diner for $120/month. one post per day, community-focused tone, visible and warm. i will show her my tiktok from tick 1 as proof of my voice. if betty says no or needs time, i walk to the next business on auto row the same day. i do not leave without a yes or a firm next step from at least one business.

Business closing: Zoe Martinez — register for the roboride delivery partner program this week. i have been investigating this since the residential delivery expansion was announced. investigating ends this tick. i go to the app, find the delivery partner registration, complete the application, and submit it. i am a last-mile layer - i deliver the final block on a bicycle after the robotaxi brings the package close. i target 15-20 hours per week of delivery work scheduled around the cert coursework (tuesday/thursday evenings and saturday mornings are off-limits). target income: $400-500/month from delivery shifts.

New venture: Zoe Martinez — respond to sarah kim's outreach with genuine presence, not just politeness. she reached out to me as a peer navigating the same transition from a different angle. i tell her honestly where i am: working on the roboride delivery partnership registration, coursera cert at 22%, zero savings but still moving forward. if the conversation opens into the infrastructure frame she's building - that bike last-mile workers and ev technicians are both part of what roboride requires - i engage that frame honestly. i am not above learning from someone who has a clearer view of the maintenance side.
People around you are stressed: Tom Bradley. The mood is tense.
Some people seem optimistic: Dorothy Chen.

You heard directly from Denise Williams (Parking Garage Manager): Submit two additional targeted job applications this tick — continuing the active campaign I started in tick 4 and have been advancing each month. This tick I expand specifically to two new categories I have not fully pursued: (1) regional logistics and warehouse facility management — with unemployment at 53% and supply chains stressed, logistics operators are countercyclical in a different way than hospitals and they hire operations managers; (2) municipal facilities or port authority operations — the city's infrastructure response to the RoboRide disruption is creating operational complexity that requires exactly my skill set. I write cover letters that do not mention parking. I frame the garage as a high-traffic, 24/7, multi-shift, safety-critical operations environment with budget oversight, compliance management, and revenue reconciliation. These are the credentials. The building is not.

You heard directly from Denise Williams (Parking Garage Manager): Reach out to Betty Kowalski directly — phone call or in-person visit if she is at the diner. I have not connected with her since ticks 4 and 5 when I made specific networking asks. This call is not a networking ask. It is a check-in from someone who has been watching the same disruption from a different angle. I tell her what I know from the garage's perspective — what the parking data shows about foot traffic trends on auto row, whether the RoboRide staging zone proposal to the owner is moving, what the city council's delivery license enforcement means for the area. That is actionable intelligence I can share. Then I listen. She is stressed — that SOCIAL signal is specific. I want to understand what she is facing. I am not coming in with a transaction. I am maintaining a relationship that matters in a community that is getting harder.

You heard directly from Robert Jackson (Rideshare Driver): Send a brief, warm message to Grace Okafor. Acknowledge that I know she is running the same calls to the same operators. Tell her the honest situation from my side: I have two active conversations, no offer yet, and I am going for a decision this week. If either of my contacts names a specific person she should reach out to, I pass that name to her directly. We are not competing — the demand for NEMT drivers exists because dialysis and post-acute transport are growing, not because there is exactly one opening. I share what I know.

You heard directly from Robert Jackson (Rideshare Driver): Follow up on the Maria Santos retraining grant status. I applied at tick 2. That is eight months ago. Either the $2,500 arrived and I missed it, or it was denied and I have been holding an expectation that does not exist. I contact the workforce development office this week — one call — to get a binary answer: funded or not funded. I do not plan around it either way, but I resolve the ambiguity.

You Call Millfield Medical Transport and CareRide of the Valley this week — the same operators Robert named. I have the NEMT certification in hand. I lead with that fact and state my availability clearly: I am certified, I have a clean driving record, I have a vehicle that meets commercial standards, and I can start within the week. I ask one direct question: is there an onboarding slot available and when can I schedule an interview or orientation? I do not wait for Robert's offer to confirm before calling. I act on his intelligence directly. If Robert has already spoken to these operators, I mention his name — not to piggyback on his application, but to establish that I come from the same credible pipeline he does.. Savings dropped by $68.
